notes: Changed: strict read-only now stops writes, not reading. With the toggle on a run can query the database with sqlcmd as well as through the two MCP servers, and still cannot write through any of them, whatever route it takes. Put the SQL on the command line where the app can see it — a query hidden behind -i, held in a variable, or wrapped in sp_executesql is refused, because a statement the app cannot read is one it cannot clear. SELECT ... INTO, BULK INSERT, OPENROWSET and xp_cmdshell are refused too; they are writes however they are dressed.

Why that changed: the old rule banned every database client outright, which also banned reading. That assumed dab-phr could answer the reads instead, and it cannot — it only reads the tables declared in its config, and adding one needs a restart. Measured: a running server still refused a newly added table after 35 seconds, while a fresh one read it instantly. So a run that met an undeclared table had no way to read it at all, and the only way out was to switch the toggle off — the one outcome worth avoiding.

Fixed: a tool call that strict read-only could not parse was allowed through instead of being refused, so a malformed call was a way past every rule in it. The tool name is unreadable in that case, so the raw text is judged instead: a write or a database client visible anywhere in it is refused, and anything else still runs.

Fixed: test screenshots were left behind in the run folder instead of going into the RCA. On one bug the whole RCA went in without a single screenshot while four passing shots sat on disk, and a second patch had to be made afterwards. The instruction existed but sat around 850 lines before the step that actually writes the RCA. It now lives where the RCA is written, and a run cannot report the RCA as finished while shots exist and the Testing field carries no image.
